records.answer: The TatarTTS dataset contains around 70 hours of speech [1], recorded by two professional speakers, one male and one female [2].

The apertium-anaphora module increased the accuracy of anaphor translation for Spanish–English by 25 percentage points (from 29.2% to 54.2%) but caused a slight decrease in accuracy for Catalan–Italian (from 83.3% to 75.0%) [1].

The apertium-recursive module was developed to deal with the limitations of finite-state chunking and to apply structural transfer rules recursively using context-free grammars (CFGs) and a Generalized Left-right Right-reduce (GLR) parser [2].
The three golden rules of fat loss in Gutless are: 1. Calories, 2. Protein, and 3. Consistency [1, 4].
A 185-pound person should eat between 1850 and 2220 calories per day to lose fat using the simple method [1].

records.answer: A 220-pound person at 25% body fat should eat approximately 180 grams of protein per day [3].

To calculate your daily calorie intake for fat loss using the simple method, first convert your weight from kilograms to pounds (80 kg x 2.2 = 176 pounds). Then multiply your weight in pounds by a number between 10 and 12. Your estimated calorie intake for fat loss would be somewhere between 1760 calories (176 x 10 = 1760) and 2112 calories (176 x 12 = 2112) per day [1].
100 grams of Quorn provides around 15 grams of protein, while 100 grams of beef mince provides around 20 grams of protein [1].
Apertium uses an unsupervised maximum entropy approach to learn weights, which allows different rules to be applied in different overlapping lexical environments [1].

Gutless says the timing of a water preload should depend on your age because younger individuals have a faster gastric emptying rate, while older individuals have a slower rate [2], which affects how effectively the water preload influences calorie intake [3].

The baseline TatarTTS models were built as a baseline for the Tatar language [1], and they were trained separately for each speaker, creating single-speaker models. Each model was trained on A100 GPUs on an NVIDIA DGX server [4]. These models were also built and evaluated using the subjective mean opinion score (MOS) measure [3].

Grapes play a role in explaining energy density as they have a low energy density, with 150 calories of raisins (which are dried grapes) being equivalent to 220 grams of grapes [2]. In the author's diet, frozen grapes are used as a dessert alternative with an energy density of 0.7, which is much lower than high-energy-dense foods like Ben & Jerry’s Peanut Butter Cup [3].
